Indian Mathematics Record
Treatise: Baudhayana Sulba Sutra (Sutra 1.48)
Author: Baudhayana
Period: c. 800 BCE - 600 BCE (Vedic Period)
Domain: geometry

HISTORICAL_FORMULA:
dīrghasyākṣaṇayā rajjuḥ pārśvamānī tiryaṅmānī ca yatpṛthagbhūte kurutastadubhayaṅ karoti (The diagonal chord of a rectangle produces both areas which the length and breadth produce separately)

MODERN_EQUIVALENT:
d^2 = l^2 + w^2 (Geometric diagonal theorem for rectangles / Pythagorean theorem in plane Euclidean geometry)

Mathematical Context: Prescribed exact geometric cord constructions for Vedic fire altars (agnicayana), including squaring the circle and doubling the square.
Historical Significance: Earliest known recorded explicit Sanskrit statement of the diagonal area relationship predating Pythagoras of Samos.
Provenance Reference: The Sulba Sutras: Texts on Vedic Geometry (G. Thibaut, Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, 1875)
